paper.title_en: Advance warning of $γ$-ray blazar flares from Fermi-LAT light curves: a strictly causal machine-learning backtest
paper.abstract_en: Long-term Fermi-LAT monitoring makes it possible to ask whether a blazar light curve shows signs of an upcoming flare before it becomes obvious in the $γ$-ray emission. We present a strictly causal machine-learning framework for forecasting $γ$-ray blazar flares from 3-d binned LAT light curves. Flare intervals are identified with Bayesian Blocks, and 42 variability features are measured from 365-d trailing windows. We train separate WATCH and TRIGGER models: WATCH predicts whether flare activity will appear within the next 90 d, while TRIGGER predicts whether a new flare onset will occur within the next 45 d. To avoid temporal leakage, all scaling, calibration, threshold selection, and validation use only pre-cutoff data (before MJD 60000). We apply the method to the FSRQ 4FGL J1048.4+7143, using 13 bright blazars as auxiliary training sources. Among logistic regression, polynomial logistic regression, and random forest classifiers, polynomial logistic regression gives the strongest held-out WATCH performance, with ROC AUC = 0.884, average precision = 0.392, and a block-permutation probability $p_{\rm perm}$ = 0.009. At the selected threshold it recovers 21 of the 21 positive WATCH windows. For TRIGGER, the same model gives AUC = 0.751, but with just nine positive test windows its AP = 0.121 is only about twice the random baseline (0.052), and no reliable pre-onset TRIGGER alert is obtained. The WATCH state appears before both held-out flares, with alerts 4.5 and 2.5 d before onset. These results suggest that the Fermi-LAT light curve of this source contains useful predictive information about its flare build-up during the period considered.
